# Data & networking development notes

> Core Data, caching, network requests, messaging, notifications and system services.

## Historical context

Historical development notes from 2015–2017. Their original publication dates and source attribution are retained; translation or catalog updates do not make the examples current.
The examples were not rerun for this reorganization. Old Swift syntax, APIs, dependencies, service addresses and App Store rules may be obsolete; check current official documentation before applying them.

## Articles by original publication date

- [Reading iOS contacts and sending SMS invitations](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2015-06-16-reading-ios-contacts-and-sending-sms-invitations/index.md): Introduces a small wrapper for a friend-invitation workflow: reading device contacts and opening the SMS composer. It lists the AddressBook, AddressBookUI and MessageUI dependencies and provides the LBContacts example project. Originally published: 2015-06-16. Published in 2015. The example depends on AddressBook and AddressBookUI. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [Getting started with XMPP, step by step](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2015-09-23-getting-started-with-xmpp-step-by-step/index.md): Records the initial integration of XMPP chat: importing dependencies, connecting to Openfire with user information, handling registration and sign-in authentication, and processing message callbacks. Client-side code accompanies the connection and messaging workflow. Originally published: 2015-09-23. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [Integrating Alipay friend sharing in three minutes](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2015-10-21-integrating-alipay-friend-sharing-in-three-minutes/index.md): Walks through app registration, SDK import, URL Scheme configuration and callbacks for sharing to Alipay friends. It distinguishes the data objects for text, image and web messages, and records checks for installation detection and authentication failures. Originally published: 2015-10-21. Uses the 2015 Alipay SocialSDK, with notes on iOS 9 Scheme configuration and Alipay Wallet 9.0. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [Using Alamofire with Swift 2.0](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2015-11-09-using-alamofire-with-swift-2-0/index.md): Shows how to import Alamofire manually, configure project dependencies and make network requests in a Swift 2.0 environment. Screenshots identify the project-linking settings, preserving an early framework integration and usage workflow. Originally published: 2015-11-09. Targets Swift 2.0 and the Alamofire APIs available at the time. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [OCR for debit and credit cards in iOS development](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2015-12-07-ocr-for-debit-and-credit-cards-in-ios-development/index.md): Introduces card.io SDK integration for scanning card numbers, including linker settings, delegates and recognition callbacks. Objective-C and Swift examples accompany the workflow; the article specifies that the selected implementation is for credit-card scanning. Originally published: 2015-12-07. Specifies Xcode 7.1 and identifies the selected solution as a credit-card scanner. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [GitHub source-code picks, January 4: Bluetooth, launch animations and a custom tab bar](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-01-04-github-source-code-picks-january-4-bluetooth-launch-animations-and-a-custom-tab-bar/index.md): Selects the BabyBluetooth framework, CLClipImageView launch animation and CYLTabBarController tab bar. Project links and selected usage examples introduce the components, including the distinction between Bluetooth central and peripheral modes. Originally published: 2016-01-04. Historical resources collected by Bison. The listed projects belong to their respective authors.
- [Understanding and using Core Data for persistence](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-01-10-understanding-and-using-core-data-for-persistence/index.md): Explains the relationship between managed objects, contexts and the persistent store coordinator, then sets up Core Data and an entity model manually. Examples of creating, fetching, updating and deleting objects illustrate the main persistence workflow. Originally published: 2016-01-10. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [Integrating LianLian Pay into an iOS app](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-01-20-integrating-lianlian-pay-into-an-ios-app/index.md): Organises the linker options, resource styles and business fields required by the LianLian Pay SDK. It explains user identifiers, card-binding agreements and server callbacks, with notes on signatures and UI customisation settings that are easy to confuse. Originally published: 2016-01-20. Published in 2016, based on the LianLian Pay SDK documentation and resource structure available then. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [Do you need Alamofire? Trying NSURLSession instead](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-01-25-do-you-need-alamofire-trying-nsurlsession-instead/index.md): Introduces NSURLSession through a simple data request, distinguishes data, download and upload tasks, and compares default, ephemeral and background configurations. It connects those choices with caching, cookies and the organisation of network tasks. Originally published: 2016-01-25. Published in 2016. The article retains the Swift syntax and NSURLSession naming used at the time. Originally credited to 大石头布; edited and archived by Bison.
- [Building a WeChat-style iOS app, part 4](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-02-03-building-a-wechat-style-ios-app-part-4/index.md): Adds cloud-storage and instant-messaging dependencies, wraps sign-in and registration methods, and records troubleshooting while querying user data. An early experiment with a password field is included as part of this historical development account. Originally published: 2016-02-03. Uses the LeanCloud-related APIs available at the time and records an experiment with a custom passWord field. It is not an account-security design. Originally credited to WzxJiang; edited and archived by Bison.
- [Building a WeChat-style iOS app, part 5](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-02-14-building-a-wechat-style-ios-app-part-5/index.md): Continues the profile and Moments screens, using AVUser for registration and sign-in and AVFile for avatar uploads. Image compression reduces transfer size, while notes document issues with a pull-down header image and refresh components. Originally published: 2016-02-14. Uses LeanCloud-related APIs and components from 2016. Originally credited to WzxJiang; edited and archived by Bison.
- [Remote notifications with JPush: a detailed integration guide](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-03-03-remote-notifications-with-jpush-a-detailed-integration-guide/index.md): Prepares remote notifications through App ID configuration, push capabilities and certificate requests, then integrates the JPush SDK. Development and production settings, certificate export and client callbacks document an early push-notification setup workflow. Originally published: 2016-03-03. Published in 2016, using the developer-portal interface, certificate workflow and JPush SDK available at the time. Originally credited to WzxJiang; edited and archived by Bison.
- [Building a WeChat-style iOS app, part 6](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-03-14-building-a-wechat-style-ios-app-part-6/index.md): Records three issues after integrating chat: matching keyboard animation parameters, managing observers as the app enters and leaves the background, and preserving sign-in state. It includes the handling code and explicitly limits the simplified automatic sign-in example. Originally published: 2016-03-14. Explicitly describes automatic sign-in as a simplified implementation that does not consider Keychain. Retained as a historical development record. Originally credited to WzxJiang; edited and archived by Bison.
- [Building a Swift local-cache library step by step](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-03-16-building-a-swift-local-cache-library-step-by-step/index.md): First distinguishes Documents, Caches, Preferences and temporary directories, then wraps a local file cache for objects, images and audio. Offline-browsing scenarios explain directory management and the approach to reading and writing cached content. Originally published: 2016-03-16. Published in 2016, using the Swift, file-management and archiving interfaces current at the time. Originally credited to 大石头布; edited and archived by Bison.
- [Combining AES encryption with Base64 encoding on iOS](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-03-30-combining-aes-encryption-with-base64-encoding-on-ios/index.md): Defines categories for NSData and NSString to demonstrate a workflow combining AES encryption and decryption with Base64 encoding. It notes that the client and server must agree on the same key and provides a complete demonstration project. Originally published: 2016-03-30. Published in 2016. The example uses a CommonCrypto category implementation from that period; Base64 serves as encoding in the workflow. Originally credited to Bison. Content is retained as published.
- [MVVM and chained network-request architecture](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-04-26-mvvm-and-chained-network-request-architecture/index.md): Begins with growing business logic in a view controller, using a sign-in decision to separate Model, ViewModel and ViewController responsibilities. It then introduces ReactiveCocoa and a chained network-request wrapper for organising business calls. Originally published: 2016-04-26. Originally credited to WzxJiang; edited and archived by Bison.
- [A first look at PhotoKit in Swift](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-05-09-a-first-look-at-photokit-in-swift/index.md): Uses a multi-photo picker to introduce PhotoKit, including the maximum selection count, returning an array of PHAsset objects and invoking a closure. The album project and learning resources document an attempt to move from AssetsLibrary to PhotoKit. Originally published: 2016-05-09. Published in 2016. It introduces PhotoKit, added in iOS 8, through Swift examples from that period. Originally credited to 大石头布; edited and archived by Bison.
- [Wrapping automatic object archiving and unarchiving on iOS](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-06-02-wrapping-automatic-object-archiving-and-unarchiving-on-ios/index.md): Starts with NSCoding and uses the runtime to enumerate instance variables and organise encoding. The WZXArchiver wrapper develops step by step, with discussion of child objects and the limits of automated storage. Originally published: 2016-06-02. Published in 2016. It uses the archiving interfaces of that period and explicitly notes incomplete support for unarchiving nested objects. Originally credited to WzxJiang; edited and archived by Bison.
- [iOS 10 Push Notifications: The Basics](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-09-27-ios-10-push-notifications-the-basics/index.md): Starts with enabling push capabilities and checking an existing project's configuration, then introduces iOS 10 notification registration, notification-center delegates, and callbacks. Third-party push integration illustrates the API changes involved in migrating older code. Originally published: 2016-09-27. The article covers the initial migration to iOS 10. Its signing and push-environment observations reflect the test conditions at that time. Originally credited to 徐不同; edited and archived by Bison.
- [iOS 10 Notifications, Part 1: Requests, Triggers, and Attachments](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-09-28-ios-10-notifications-part-1-requests-triggers-and-attachments/index.md): Uses local notifications to explain the relationship between UNNotificationRequest, triggers, and the notification center. It manages additions, updates, and deletions through identifiers and introduces valid file paths and configuration for notification attachments. Originally published: 2016-09-28. The article covers the UserNotifications APIs in iOS 10. Originally credited to 徐不同; edited and archived by Bison.
- [iOS 10 Notifications, Part 2: Service Extensions](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2016-10-12-ios-10-notifications-part-2-service-extensions/index.md): Explains how a Notification Service Extension processes content before a notification appears. It covers creating an extension target, changing text, loading attachments, and falling back to the original notification when processing times out. Originally published: 2016-10-12. The article covers Notification Service Extension as introduced in iOS 10. Originally credited to 徐不同; edited and archived by Bison.
- [Reading CocoaAsyncSocket: Connection Setup](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2017-02-17-reading-cocoaasyncsocket-connection-setup/index.md): Follows GCDAsyncSocket initialization and connection entry points through the CocoaAsyncSocket source. It traces parameter checks, local and server address creation, and socket configuration before connecting, using annotated code to explain the call sequence. Originally published: 2017-02-17. Published in 2017, this source walkthrough refers to the CocoaAsyncSocket implementation used in the article. Originally credited to 涂耀辉; edited and archived by Bison.
- [Reading CocoaAsyncSocket: Completing the Connection](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2017-03-09-reading-cocoaasyncsocket-completing-the-connection/index.md): Continues tracing the CocoaAsyncSocket connection process from local-address binding to connection establishment and callbacks. Low-level socket operations explain the order of asynchronous execution and the purpose of the relevant configuration. Originally published: 2017-03-09. Published in 2017, this installment follows the source version used in the preceding article. Both originals list the same source link. Originally credited to 涂耀辉; edited and archived by Bison.
- [DNS Hijacking and Request Handling in iOS](https://allluckly.cn/en/journal/2017-05-03-dns-hijacking-and-request-handling-in-ios/index.md): Introduces DNS hijacking through unexpected name-resolution results, then describes using NSURLProtocol to adjust requests and resolution. It discusses compatibility boundaries involving IPv6, WebKit, and NSURLSession and retains the implementation examples and references. Originally published: 2017-05-03. Published in 2017, the request-interception and resolution approaches should be read in light of the framework limitations of that period. Originally credited to SindriLin; edited and archived by Bison.
